executive_summary: This chapter teaches classical practical geometry using strictly an unmarked ruler and compass. Key constructions include: perpendicular bisector of a line segment, 90° angle at a point on a line, angle bisector, copying an angle (SSS application), parallel lines via equal corresponding angles, 60°/120° angles via equilateral triangle construction, 30°/15° angles via angle bisection, pointed arches, and regular hexagons (decomposed into 6 equilateral triangles around 360° center point). The second part explores Tiling (tessellations) and Tangram 7-piece puzzles.
key_takeaways: Bisection: Dividing a geometric quantity (segment, angle) into two identical equal parts.
Regular Hexagon Interior Angle: Each interior angle = 120°; composed of 6 equilateral triangles.
Tangram: 7-piece dissection puzzle originating in China consisting of 5 triangles, 1 square, 1 parallelogram.
